text: The original attention mechanism divides the query‑key dot products by a constant (specifically \(1/\sqrt{d_k}\)) before applying softmax to prevent the dot products from becoming too large when the dimensionality \(d_k\) is large. Large dot products push the softmax into regions with very small gradients, which hampers learning. Scaling the dot products keeps their magnitude in a range where the softmax has useful gradients [C:attention:18][C:attention:21][C:attention:20]

The Depth Transformer in Moshi has **6 layers** and a **model dimension of 1024** [C:moshi:82].

The smoothing module in H‑Net addresses the difficulty of training a dynamic chunking module caused by the discrete, uncertain chunk‑boundary decisions. By interpolating representations at low‑confidence boundaries, it attenuates the effect of uncertain splits, prevents misalignment during upsampling, and stabilises training dynamics, enabling the model to learn optimal chunk boundaries through gradient descent. [C:dynchunk:14] [C:dynchunk:131] [C:dynchunk:50]

The hierarchical network (H‑Net) is organized into three distinct stages: an **outer stage** that captures fine‑grained patterns, an **inner stage** that operates on coarser, token‑like representations, and a **main network** that contains the bulk of the parameters and performs the core modeling. [C:dynchunk:13]

Moshi’s Inner Monologue is a training and inference strategy that first predicts time‑aligned text tokens as a prefix to audio tokens, allowing the model to generate speech in a hierarchical, per‑frame manner while remaining compatible with streaming inference. This method improves linguistic quality, enables streaming TTS and ASR, and boosts spoken‑dialogue performance with only a modest increase in inference cost [C:moshi:3][C:moshi:29][C:moshi:253]
